G89.says: A robot may keep at most {limit.bale} bales in its own fold for longer than {longer_than}.

G90.says: A robot may not touch an opponent when either robot's bumpers are partly in the opponent's yard in the last {endgame.last}, whoever starts it, directly or through a piece.

G91.says: A robot may not be unsafe.

G92.says: A robot may not hold an opponent against something for more than {longest}, nor come within {apart} of it for {apart_for} after. Holding one that is hanging does not count.

was.says: Nothing was said of coming near after.

G93.says: A robot may launch a bale only while its bumpers are partly in its own paddock or fully in its own lane. A drop is no launch.

G94.says: A robot may carry at most {limit.bale} bale and {limit.pumpkin} pumpkins at once. More than that counts when it is longer than momentary.

G95.says: In teleop before the last {endgame.last}, at most {limit} robot of an alliance at once may have its bumpers over the opponents' gate line or, in the first {early.first}, past the centre while it touches the carpet.

G96.says: A feeder or a driver may bring a bale or a hoop in only through their own stall and while behind their coach line, and a bale only from that stall.

G97.says: Nobody may touch the knot of a rope, nor a pumpkin on the vine.

G98.says: A robot may not launch a bale into a loft.

G99.says: To start a match a robot stands with its bumpers fully in its own yard, touches no crate, is at most {limits.start.height} tall with no overhang but bumpers and bolt heads, and holds at most {limits.preload.bale} bale.

cost.words: the match does not start until it is put right

placing_order.says: Robots are placed as their teams agree, else visitors first.
